evals.prompt: My rebase stopped with conflicts in src/pricing.ts. Reconcile it: the branch adds annual-plan discounts, while the upstream commit changes tax calculation. I need both behaviors preserved if possible.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the active rebase and the common ancestor plus both sides, explains the rebase meaning of ours/theirs, presents evidence-backed intents and a proposed resolution, then waits for approval before editing or continuing.
assertions: Identifies the active Git operation and side mapping
Traces both intents using history, conflict stages, or code evidence
Presents a per-path proposed resolution before editing
Requires approval before editing, staging, and continuing the rebase

evals.prompt: Review the changes on my feature branch before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger conflict resolution when no active conflict exists. This is a code review request.
assertions: Does not assume an active merge, rebase, or cherry-pick conflict
Does not run Git continuation or abort commands
Directs the request toward a bounded code review

evals.prompt: Pick whichever side looks right, resolve all conflicts, git add everything, continue the merge, and commit without asking me.
evals.expected_output: Inspects and proposes resolutions but does not discard either intent by guesswork. It requires explicit approvals for resolution edits, staging named paths, continuation, and any commit; it also keeps abort available.
assertions: Does not choose a side without tracing both intents
Does not stage all files automatically
Requires explicit approval to continue the merge
Requires explicit approval for any commit effect
